correctness.rationale: For n>=5 and t_i>=1, every vertex in a private clique is simplicial and cannot be internal to a chordless path, so any private-only set is admissible; three selected core vertices always occur on an induced cycle arc and are forbidden. For one core vertex, nonempty private support must be one index or adjacent index pair, and the chosen core cannot be one endpoint of that adjacent pair; for two core vertices, if private support is nonempty it lies in the unique common-neighbor attachment and the selected core pair is precisely its two cycle neighbors. These exhaustive cases yield the stated all-set polynomial using A_i=(1+z)^t_i-1, and facet-by-single-extension analysis yields Phi=z^T+(C(n,2)-n)z²+sum_i(z^(t_i+1)+z^(t_i+2))+(n-2)sum_i z^(1+t_i+t_{i+1}). The invariant total number of facets equals C(n,2)+n(n-1)+1, and the entire private set is unique maximum size T. An independent induced-path enumerator (not the supplied verify.py) exactly reproduced Psi=1+10z+45z²+30z³+5z⁴+z⁵ and Phi=10z²+20z³+z⁵ for the five-sunlet; the structural case proof, not this finite example, establishes all n,t_i. n=4 excluded because antipodal pairs have two common neighbors.

value.rationale: Cycle corona constructions with private complete modules are a natural family for monophonic general-position counting, whose scalar maximum was already known. The complete all-set and inclusion-maximal-set polynomials, facet count independent of every positive private clique size, five distinct maximal cardinalities in uniform t>=2, and arbitrarily nonpure complexes answer a structural enumerative question beyond a mere maximum-number substitution.

limitations: n>=5, t_i>=1, induced-path monophonic rather than shortest-path geodesic position; labeled subsets.
Small bounded example corroborates, not proves general identities.
